review: First reasoned review of c9018dd5dbb9, bac398da6239 and 75c3098ba531
method: atomscan and cleave facts on every original; data-only Java stream parsing; rizin function disassembly and PE resource extraction. No sample code executed. ML, labels and sandbox scores were leads only.

provenance.disclosure_check: Retrieved primary disclosure with curl after the web reader failed. It describes the same HashSet/TiedMapEntry/LazyMap/ConstantTransformer/AspectJ write chain and Parasoft web-root execution sink. Its cited 2076-byte carrier is not byte-identical to this 1178-byte specimen; no exact hash corroboration is claimed.
provenance.triage: https://tria.ge/261020-rnqmvs1sht was inaccessible through the web reader; its score was not used as proof.
provenance.deployment: No machine execution logs, operator authorization or provenance tying the Java payload to an authorized test was supplied. Neither Windows specimen can be assumed operational from the surviving bytes.

java_analysis.framing: AC ED 00 05; TC_BLOCKDATA integer 1; one HashSet with one TiedMapEntry element. Decoded all 1178 bytes with a data-only parser that never resolves or loads Java classes.
object_relationships: LazyMap.factory = ConstantTransformer; iConstant is a 475-byte byte array containing JSP source.
LazyMap decorated map is SimpleCache$StoreableCachingMap with empty inherited HashMap data.
java_analysis.effect: HashSet.readObject hashes its element; TiedMapEntry.hashCode/getValue calls LazyMap.get; the absent key invokes the constant transformer and decorated map.put. AspectJ StoreableCachingMap.put writes the byte array under folder/key. In the documented vulnerable server this deposits a JSP in the web root before a later backup-type cast can reject the object.
java_analysis.jsp_effect: An HTTP visit compiles/runs the page: ProcessBuilder launches /bin/sh -c with fixed echo/id/hostname/pwd/ls diagnostics, merges stderr, transfers child stdout to ByteArrayOutputStream, waits, and prints it to the HTTP response.
java_analysis.limits: This is a fixed diagnostic exploit probe. There is no request-controlled command parameter, credential theft, reverse shell, or interactive webshell. File creation requires the relevant libraries, an unsafe deserialization entry point and a writable destination; shell execution additionally requires JSP serving.
java_analysis.judgment: MALICIOUS as a crafted exploitation artifact: the linked object graph writes executable server content outside the database restore semantics and the page executes a shell under the server principal. Authorized testing remains possible. Its proof-of-concept context and fixed diagnostics justify suspicious trait severity rather than inventing hostile webshell capabilities.

windows_analysis.shared_code: Both specimens have byte-identical .text SHA256 b217b42df0cae3844f0753e982150b0859aab02659c8618f723990def2655d86 and byte-identical .data. Imported API slots contain resolved addresses and an overwritten UUID region, consistent with damaged memory-derived images, not proof of a runnable on-disk loader.
windows_analysis.entry_and_modes: CRT entry 0x402674 calls main dispatcher 0x401cb0. Configuration dword at 0x404120 is 3 in both, selecting Active Setup copy/patch and cleanup. Other surviving branches implement ServiceDLL replacement, service installation and DLL injection. Alternate branches are code capabilities, not observed execution.
paths: 0x401900 generates a GUID via 0x401840, builds a system-directory .exe path, creates HKLM Active Setup Installed Components/<GUID>, writes StubPath, reads its own image via CRT I/O, patches configuration, writes the clone and starts it. Original file offsets patched by the code differ from memory-derived IAT layout, another reason not to assert successful reinstallation.

0x401260 opens HKLM SYSTEM/CurrentControlSet/Services/LanmanServer/Parameters; 0x401320 calls RegDeleteValueA for ServiceDLL; 0x40133e calls RegSetValueExA for the same value with REG_EXPAND_SZ and a 128-byte buffer. This distinct replacement function is separate from the ServiceDLL query in main at 0x401d35.
0x402460 locates resource type DLL/id 101, loads and copies its bytes, then calls file writer 0x4023c0. Main links the drop path to replacement and 0x401150 injection.

0x401150 selects iexplore/notepad/calc via 0x4010c0, creates the process, allocates remote memory, writes a DLL path, resolves Kernel32.LoadLibraryA, and passes the export and remote buffer to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.
0x401390 gets the current module and its short path, reads COMSPEC, constructs /c del <self> > nul, creates the shell process and adjusts priorities/resumes its thread.
windows_analysis.bac_damage: Resource directory and mapped .rsrc region are erased. The extra 32020 bytes beyond the mapped image contain data/Windows licensing records; no execution transfer into the overlay was established. Missing resources prevent the resource-drop branch from obtaining its DLL.
windows_analysis.75c_damage: Resource DLL/101/2052 is 39936 bytes at outer offset 0x5060. Its entry RVA 0x741a is zero-filled, executable sections/imports are absent, and only data strings and headers remain. Family command/HTTP/DNS strings do not establish live C2, downloading or DDoS code.
windows_analysis.judgment: Both MALICIOUS: family banners corroborate the traced core-service replacement, clandestine reactivation, remote DLL loading and cleanup design. Damage limits execution, but does not change that surviving design. The collector labels WannaCry and Remcos are not supported family identifications for these bytes.

changes: Replace three suspicious ordinary class-name matches under exploitation with notable, byte-framed Java serialization descriptor observations; add Java stream magic and HashSet/AspectJ descriptors.

Require the complete write-gadget type set and stream framing for one suspicious graph finding. Require JSP shell/child-stream/HTTP output context for the second suspicious probe finding. Neither requires a generated filename, product path or sample token.

Retire the generic two-call fragment and family-gated persistence composite. Add an API-bound, same-value-pointer ServiceDLL delete/rewrite capability under registry/write; reference it with LanmanServer/resource/injection context under service persistence. Retain the independent family identity finding.

At the 100-rule registry/write budget, the audit identified CrashControl key text incorrectly filed as a write. Move its unchanged matcher/scope to keys/policy, remove unsupported inherited T1112, and update both direct consumers. No directory limit was increased or split for capacity.
reference_audit: No other active YAML consumers referenced the removed Java atoms or StormAttack fragment/composite. The new serialization atoms have no existing broad serialization consumers. The magic ancestor consumer is PHP code-in-image with disjoint JPEG/PNG scope. The moved CrashControl path has two updated exact consumers and no keys/policy or keys-only directory consumer. Registry/write directory consumers retain their behavior guards; the new bound writer is already a subset of existing RegSetValueExA coverage on these samples. Registry-wide membership is retained for CrashControl.
